questions.stem: Which claim about honorific speech is NOT correct?

options.text: Honorifics in Japanese are expressed only by raising the pitch of the voice.
Respect is shown in Japanese solely by using Chinese loanwords.
options.misconception: confuses which of these claims about honorific speech is actually accurate

options.text: Japanese honorifics mark respect through special verb forms, humble forms, and polite endings such as です and ます.
options.misconception: confuses which of these claims about honorific speech is actually accurate

options.text: Japanese has no grammatical way to show respect to a listener.
options.misconception: confuses which of these claims about honorific speech is actually accurate

questions.explanation: The statement identified as NOT correct is inaccurate because Honorifics in Japanese are expressed only by raising the pitch of the voice.. By contrast, the accurate claim about honorific speech is: Japanese honorifics mark respect through special verb forms, humble forms, and polite endings such as です and ます. Keigo is a graded system: sonkeigo elevates the subject, kenjougo humbles the speaker, and teineigo marks general politeness. Distinguishing a true description from a plausible false one is the point of this item.
